vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: privacy-policy
Version: 1.0.7

The skill bundle is a legitimate utility for generating privacy policy templates (GDPR, CCPA, and standard) and providing basic security checklists. The primary logic is contained in `scripts/privacy.sh`, which uses heredocs to output text templates based on user-provided parameters like company name and email. A secondary script, `scripts/script.sh`, provides placeholder security commands such as `scan`, `audit`, and `harden`, which primarily log actions to a local directory (`~/.local/share/privacy-policy`). No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized network access, or malicious intent was found in the code or instructions.

llm.summary: The package mostly matches a privacy-policy generator, but it contains an unexpected security-scanning/hardening script that writes logs to the user's data directory and some minor inconsistencies in commands — this mismatch is unexplained and worth caution.

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose is a privacy policy generator; scripts/privacy.sh implements that. However, scripts/script.sh is a separate 'security scanning and hardening' tool (scan/audit/harden/encrypt/hash/password/etc.) unrelated to generating privacy policies. Bundling an unrelated tool is incoherent with the stated purpose and not justified in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running privacy-policy style commands (generate, gdpr, ccpa, app, website, audit). The included scripts will create a data directory and write logs (DATA_DIR/history.log, data.log) under $PRIVACY_POLICY_DIR or ~/.local/share/privacy-policy. SKILL.md does not disclose that files will be written to the user's home directory. There are no network endpoints or credential reads, and no explicit exfiltration, but the file-write behavior is not documented in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or external downloads are present; the skill is delivered as local script files only, so there is no remote code fetching. This lowers install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. scripts/script.sh honors PRIVACY_POLICY_DIR and XDG_DATA_HOME and falls back to $HOME; reading $HOME and respecting an optional $PRIVACY_POLICY_DIR is reasonable, but users should note the default data directory used.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or elevated privileges, but scripts/script.sh will create and write files under a per-user data directory (~/.local/share/privacy-policy by default). This is persistent state on disk that the SKILL.md does not call out explicitly.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to include a legitimate privacy-policy generator (scripts/privacy.sh) but also bundles an unrelated security-scanning/hardening script (scripts/script.sh) that will create a per-user data directory and append logs there. Before installing or running: 1) Inspect the two scripts locally — especially script.sh — to confirm you want that extra functionality and file writes. 2) If you only need the policy generator, consider removing or not executing script.sh. 3) Run the scripts in a sandboxed environment (or with a non-critical account) first to observe behavior. 4) Check that no network calls are added before running in a production environment. 5) Remember the generated policies are template guidance — consult a qualified lawyer for legal compliance. If you want a firmer verdict, provide confirmation from the publisher about why the security tool is bundled or a copy of any network/telemetry behavior logs.
